title: Katherine Ryan Called Russell Brand a ‘Sexual Predator’ on Comedy Central in 2018. She’s Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ After Brand Convicted of Rape
description: Years after Katherine Ryan reportedly confronted Russell Brand about alleged predatory behavior while working alongside him on Comedy Central’s “Ro
body:
Years after Katherine Ryan reportedly confronted Russell Brand about alleged predatory behavior while working alongside him on Comedy Central’s “Roast Battle” in 2018, the comedian has spoken out following his conviction on rape and sexual assault charges.

	“It really made me feel just quite dysregulated again, caught off-guard, emotional, in awe of the survivors who also had nothing to gain,” Ryan said on the latest episode of her podcast “Telling Everybody Everything.” “They came forward despite Russell Brand having fame, power, money and a legion of fans ready to attack them.”
	

	The Canadian comedian said she and other women had been privately processing the verdict, which she described as bringing both a sense of justice and renewed grief for those affected.

	“I will never be someone who like, dances on graves. There has been some justice done today,” she said. “There’s a level of relief, but there’s grief alongside relief.”

	She continued: “Everything’s nuanced, and it was proved in court that a terrible thing happened, and that means that a terrible thing happened.”

	Ryan previously made headlines in 2022 when she told Louis Theroux in his BBC documentary series that she had confronted an unnamed male comedian about his alleged predatory behavior. During the interview, Ryan said she had worked alongside a man on a television program and called him a “predator,” describing the potential legal repercussions as a “litigious minefield.”

	Her comments fueled speculation that she was referring to Brand. Ryan has never publicly confirmed the identity of the comedian she was discussing.
	

	Brand, 51, was found guilty Thursday of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault following a four-week trial at London’s Southwark Crown Court. He was acquitted of two additional rape charges and one count of indecent assault. The comedian, who denied all allegations of non-consensual sexual activity, is scheduled to be sentenced on Monday.

schema.headline: Katherine Ryan Called Russell Brand a ‘Sexual Predator’ on Comedy Central in 2018. She’s Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ After Brand Convicted of Rape

description:

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Lego is bringing together some of the biggest names in entertainment for its new holiday campaign, directed by “The Greatest Showman” and “Better Man” filmmaker Michael Gracey.

	Set to Daft Punk’s 2000 hit “One More Time,” the 74-second commercial takes viewers inside a fantastical Lego workshop, where characters from across the toy company’s sprawling universe work together to create the perfect holiday gift. Among those making appearances are Marvel superheroes Thor, Doctor Doom and Mystique, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Derpy Tiger from Netflix’s “KPop Demon Hunters” and the French electronic music duo themselves.


	“I loved the concept that behind this secret door, there might be an entire world you never knew existed and with Lego bricks, that world really could be anything,” director Michael Gracey said in a statement. “We decided to tell the story through the eyes of one little Lego brick, following its journey through this extraordinary workshop as it passes from one character to the next.”

	The campaign arrives just weeks after Lego announced a new partnership with Daft Punk, spanning products, content and live experiences. The collaboration, unveiled Oct. 22, includes an upcoming Lego Ideas set recreating the duo’s iconic pyramid stage from their 2007 “Alive” tour. Originally submitted by a father-and-son team from Luxembourg, the fan-designed model has been approved for development, with more details expected in 2027.

	The holiday campaign is also the latest example of Lego’s growing investment in entertainment-driven collaborations. In August, the company released a 1,478-piece set inspired by “The X-Files.” Gillian Anderson, who played Dana Scully in the original sci-fi series, returned for a promotional short film celebrating the release.

title: ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ Sets Collectors Edition Featuring Miley Cyrus Q&A and Deleted Scenes
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	James Cam
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	James Cameron is inviting audiences back to Pandora with a new collector’s edition of “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” arriving on digital platforms and 4K Ultra HD on Dec. 8.

	The special release, available on Prime Video, will feature more than nine hours of bonus material, including deleted and extended scenes, behind-the-scenes footage and an awards-season conversation with Miley Cyrus, who contributed the film’s end-title ballad, “Dream as One.”
	

	The newly released footage includes scenes exploring the relationship between Jake Sully (Sam Worthington) and Neytiri (Zoe Saldaña), as well as additional storylines involving their children and returning antagonist Colonel Miles Quaritch (Stephen Lang). One deleted sequence sees Jake and Spider held captive at the RDA’s Bridgehead facility, while others follow Lo’ak’s pursuit of Payakan, the Sully family’s escape from the Ash People and an alternate death for General Ardmore.

	The edition will also feature “Fire and Water: Making the Avatar Films,” a two-part behind-the-scenes documentary, along with performance-capture demonstrations featuring Worthington, Sigourney Weaver, Lang and Oona Chaplin. Additional extras include scene breakdowns, cast and filmmaker panels, and tribute to late “Avatar” producer Jon Landau.

	The physical edition will also include archival material, including the screenplay and production art.

	Released theatrically in December 2025, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” marked the third installment in Cameron’s blockbuster franchise, following 2009’s “Avatar” and 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water.” The film follows Jake and Neytiri as they navigate the aftermath of their family’s losses while confronting a new Na’vi clan known as the Ash People, led by Chaplin’s Varang.
	

	The sequel grossed $1.5 billion worldwide and an Academy Award for best visual effects. 

	The “Avatar: Fire and Ash” Collector’s Edition will be available Dec. 8.

schema.headline: ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ Sets Collectors Edition Featuring Miley Cyrus Q&A and Deleted Scenes

title: From ‘World of Warcraft Forever’ Surprise to Le Sserafim, Simu Liu and T-Pain Appearances, How BlizzCon 2026 Set the Stage for Blizzard Entertainment’s Next Era
description: Back in September, Blizzard Entertainment held its fan convention BlizzCon for the first time since 2023, just after Activision Blizzard was acquir
body:
Back in September, Blizzard Entertainment held its fan convention BlizzCon for the first time since 2023, just after Activision Blizzard was acquired by Microsoft in a blockbuster $69 billion transaction, which signaled a renewed investment in gaming by the software giant, from Sept. 12 to the 13. 

	BlizzCon drew 35,000 in-person attendees to the Anaheim Convention Center and racked up 12.5 million live viewers for the event. Less than two months later, Blizzard is celebrating the launch of “World of Warcraft Forever,” a title first announced on stage during the live show in September to much fanfare.
	

	For this week’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business,” Jennifer Maas was on the ground at BlizzCon 2026 speaking with Blizzard Entertainment president Johanna Faries, “World of Warcraft Forever” game director Ion Hazzikostas, celebrity attendees including Simu Liu, T-Pain, and the members of K-pop sensation Le Sserafim about the festivities and what this moment means for the future of Blizzard. 

	LISTEN to the full conversation on Variety’s “Strictly Business” podcast:

	“We were even backstage and we’ve seen all the show and all said it feels like we were watching it for the first time all over again because we are finally sharing it with our players in our community,” Faries says, just off the main stage where Blizzard had made a slew of announcements, including “Diablo 5” is coming in spring 2029, a new “StarCraft” open-world shooter is coming in 2030, a Netflix animated adaptation of ‘”Diablo” is in the works, and “World of Warcraft Forever” would be out Nov. 4.
	

	“Strictly Business” is Variety’s weekly podcast featuring conversations with industry leaders about the business of media and entertainment. (Please click here to subscribe to our free newsletter.) New episodes debut every Friday and can be downloaded at Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, Spotify, Google Play, SoundCloud and more.

schema.headline: From ‘World of Warcraft Forever’ Surprise to Le Sserafim, Simu Liu and T-Pain Appearances, How BlizzCon 2026 Set the Stage for Blizzard Entertainment’s Next Era

title: A24’s ‘It Gets Worse’ Updates ‘Girls’ for British Gen Z: TV Review
description: The series “It Gets Worse” is a star vehicle for its 20-something writer-creator that skewers a dysfunctional friend group flailing about in a big
body:
The series “It Gets Worse” is a star vehicle for its 20-something writer-creator that skewers a dysfunctional friend group flailing about in a big city. Though there are important distinctions — the protagonist is a gay man, not all the main characters are white and the action unfolds in London rather than the Big Apple — the influence of “Girls” is unmistakable. But by the time the parallels really sink in, “It Gets Worse” has beaten you to the punch. Yes, an underemployed striver being told their internship won’t result in the professional boost they were hoping for is a story beat straight out of Lena Dunham’s magnum opus. This time, however, the boss breaking the bad news is played by Dunham herself.Leo Reich, the lead and creative voice of “It Gets Worse,” collaborated with Dunham on her Netflix show “Too Much,” in which he played one of the heroine’s chaotic co-workers. It’s possible Dunham saw a kindred spirit in the comedian, another precocious child of urban creatives (Reich’s father is a film producer) with a keen eye for his peers’ self-delusion. If Hannah Horvath was a voice of a generation, a joke that’s slowly acquired a ring of earnestness as “Girls” has passed the test of time, then Dunham’s cameo marks a passing of the baton from millennials to Gen Z.Originally produced by the über-hip studio A24 for the U.K.’s Channel 4, where the show premiered last month and will air on Paramount+ in the U.S., “It Gets Worse” clocks in at a tight and typically British half-dozen episodes. As such, the plot zeroes in on a suitably narrow slice of time: the window between college friends turned roommates Ethan (Reich), Abi (Emily Fairn) and Sam (Olive Gray) having to move out of one apartment — sorry, flat — and signing a lease on another. Whether they’ll actually relocate is an open question given the trio’s poor collective decision-making. Selfish, hapless Ethan gets too distracted by internet scrolling to fix a hole in the wall and loses their security deposit, much to Sam’s ire. Abi actually wants to move in with her boyfriend, Tom (Sean Delaney), but can’t bring herself to tell the others. Sam, an aspiring writer, supplements her Substack essays with standardized test tutoring that still may not be enough to cover London rent.
	

	Everyone’s inner monologue is narrated by no less than author Zadie Smith, whose voice-over’s cool assurance forms a productive contrast with the characters’ anxious scrambling. (When Dunham’s girlboss tells Abi she apologizes too much, the younger woman’s first instinct is to say she’s sorry.) Reich suffers slightly from the paradox of early comedic success: Failure is funny, so Ethan is a hot mess while the person playing him counts Pulitzer finalist Smith — plus Dunham and BAFTA winner Andrew Scott, also a guest star — as a collaborator. Yet “It Gets Worse” is on point enough in its diagnosis of generational malaise that the irony quickly fades.

	“Ethan had one of the easiest lives in recorded human history,” Smith begins. But that relative comfort has only provided more opportunities for self-sabotage. Abi seems to like the lifestyle that comes with settled monogamy more than her actual boyfriend. (The foodie satire, like the portrait of Anthony Bourdain Tom hangs in the kitchen, cuts particularly deep.) Ethan chases after straight guys who treat him like shit. Sam is hung up on an ex who invites her to crash at a queer commune that hosts sex parties with consent forms. Not all their problems — see Brexit — are of their own making, but many are. As the title suggests, “It Gets Worse” has pessimism baked in from the jump. Yet the show’s resigned nihilism, softened with gallows humor, takes after Ethan, who once contemplated suicide but found sourcing enough paracetamol too much of a hassle. What’s left except to muddle through?

schema.headline: A24’s ‘It Gets Worse’ Updates ‘Girls’ for British Gen Z: TV Review

title: Motorhead’s Classic ‘Orgasmatron’ Gets a Mighty 40th Anniversary Sonic Upgrade and Deluxe Edition: Album Review
description: The best rock bands create their greatest work with their backs against the wall — witness the Rolling Stones — and the legendary British hard-rock
body:
The best rock bands create their greatest work with their backs against the wall — witness the Rolling Stones — and the legendary British hard-rock powerhouse Motorhead was no exception.

	Forty years ago, the band had seen the dissolution of its classic “No Sleep ‘Til Hammersmith” lineup accompanied by a pair of sub-par studio albums, and had been largely given up for dead. But the band’s leader, Lemmy Kilmister, was nothing if not a survivor. He regrouped with a pair of blazing guitarists and thunderous ex-Saxon drummer Pete Gill and, for this album, joined forces with the unexpected choice of producer Bill Laswell, who was well known in experimental-leaning New York rock/jazz circles — and producer Herbie Hancock’s left-field 1983 hit “Rockit” — but seemed an odd fit for Motorhead.
	

	However, Laswell had been experimenting with hard rock at the time, and he came to Motorhead fresh from overseeing the pioneering 1984 rap-rock fusion, John Lydon and Afrika Bambaata’s “World Destruction,” as well as Public Image Ltd.’s fiery “Album,” which united Lydon with a wide-ranging band including guitar wizard Steve Vai, ex-Cream drummer Ginger Baker and Funkadelic’s Bernie Worrell.

	The result of this unlikely union was “Orgasmatron,” certainly Motorhead’s most experimental album and one that drew a polarized reaction from many fans and the band itself — the press materials for this reissue euphemistically state, “The album’s production was the subject of much discussion among the band and their fans” — who said its mix was too cluttered and took the band too far from the basics. But personally speaking, I loved it and still do.
	

	In an era when music fans were much more tribal than today, Motorhead were one of the rare bands who were respected in both punk and heavy metal circles. Like AC/DC, their earlier music was rock and roll stripped down to muscle and bone — scorching guitars, piledriving drums and Lemmy’s vein-bulging roar of a voice — like a Terminator version of Chuck Berry. And on “Orgasmatron,” we got all of that in a more-adventurous sonic setting: The songs are classic Motorhead, but hazy guitar overdubs, percussion and effects swoop in and out of the mix, especially on the closing title track, a cauldron of seething guitars, driving drums and Lemmy’s voice, which is laden with effects that make him sound like Darth Vader and Vecna morphed together. The song is like molten lava in musical form, and includes Lemmy’s best-ever lyrics: “I am the one, Orgasmatron, the outstretched grasping hand/ My image is of agony, my servants rape the land/ Obsequious and arrogant, clandestine and vain/ Two thousand years of misery, of torture in my name.” (The song

	Subsequent re-releases have punched up the mix, and this new 40th anniversary edition presents not only a remastered version of Laswell’s original mix, but a 2026 remix from the band’s longtime latter-day producer Cameron Webb that clears away some of the haze and presents the guitars and drums in cleaner sound (although to be honest it doesn’t sound radically different). They’ve also cleaned out the vault, adding some rehearsal tapes (which sound like they were recorded on a boombox), an outtake and a BBC session featuring several songs from the album along with the classic “Killed by Death” — as well as Lemmy reading the lyrics to the song “Orgasmatron,” unaccompanied, like some sort of evil poet.

	Despite the polarized reaction to the original mix, “Orgasmatron” proved definitively that Motorhead were back, and the band launched into its second golden era in earnest. And the band got back to basics soon enough: Classic-era drummer Phil Taylor returned the following year for the “Rock N’ Roll” album, which marked a return to their usual sound and production, and the band roared off into the sunset, only disbanding after Lemmy’s death in 2015 at the age of 75.

	While the bonus tracks here are nice to have but not necessarily electrifying, the remastered and otherwise soup-ed up sound on the original album makes this one of the top reissues of the year — “Orgasmatron” now roars louder than ever.
	

	—

schema.headline: Motorhead’s Classic ‘Orgasmatron’ Gets a Mighty 40th Anniversary Sonic Upgrade and Deluxe Edition: Album Review

title: Jim Cramer Leads CNBC Into Creator-Media Era
description:
CNBC is investing more heavily in Jim Cramer.

	The former hedge-fund manager, who leads the business-news outlet’s “Mad Money” and co-anchors “Squ
body:
CNBC is investing more heavily in Jim Cramer.

	The former hedge-fund manager, who leads the business-news outlet’s “Mad Money” and co-anchors “Squawk on the Street,” will expand the investing club he hosts via CNBC, launching a premium tier in 2027 that gives subscribers new access to live shows and workshops he plans to lead. CNBC plans to hire a general manager to help Cramer run the operation, and will unveil pricing and membership details at a later date. Cramer is branching out as part of a new long-term contract with CNBC that extends his relationship with the Versant-backed outlet.
	

	The club, says Cramer during a recent interview, “can fulfill what I feel is my life’s mission, which is to try to help people make money, try to help people learn about investing.” He’s been able to do that with a regular presence on CNBC for about a quarter century, and, he says, “I don’t tire of it.”

	CNBC has offered Jim Cramer’s Investing Club since 2022, giving members access to the trades that are made for his Charitable Trust; analysis of the stocks it holds; videos; daily market analysi; and monthly virtual meetings. On Friday, some members will gather for an annual meeting of the club in downtown Manhattan.

	And though Cramer has been talking to CNBC aficionados for years, he is helping the network and its corporate parent dive into something extremely au courant. More people are gravitating to experts, independent journalists and so-called “creators” who rely on interactive media such as digital newsletters and video podcasts to forge relationships with followers. With Cramer, CNBC is showing that traditional media can also play in that arena.
	

	“This is very indicative of where media is going,” says KC Sullivan, president of CNBC, during an interview. “It’s about super-serving super-passionate audiences.”

	Other traditional media outlets have begun to experiment with similar ideas. Comcast’s Sky News recently launched a new mobile app focused on defense and security, with top sector reporters at its center. Subscriptions to the new “Defence Insider” cost £14.99 per month — about $20.31 in U.S. dollars, more than the fees for a similar subscription to CNN or Fox Nation. Indeed, the price of getting “Defence Insider” is on par with the highest-cost monthly dues for HBO Max or Netflix.

	Meanwhile, MS NOW, a CNBC sibling, has launched a subscription “Membership:” service that gives followers access to interactive chats with personalities like Rachel Maddow, Nicolle Wallace or the team from “Morning Joe.”

	Under CEO Mark Lazarus, Versant has placed particular emphasis on developing a suite of direct-to-consumer products that range from services that cater to golf fans who might watch the company’s Golf Channel, to users of Fandango, the movie-ticketing service recently expanded to include ad-supported streaming video. Versant has articulated a strategy of getting half of its revenue from digital and direct-to-consumer businesses so as to reduce its dependency on the traditional cable networks at the core of its operations.

	In its most recent quarter, Versant said traditional advertising revenue dipped 5.3% while fees from distribution were off 5.8%. Revenue from its non-TV operations, however, rose 9.6%.

	Cramer is, in a sense, leading the charge, and he thinks his work can continue uninterrupted by sticking with CNBC, rather than lighting out for digital territory on his own. “It would lack the infrastructure” that CNBC brings, he says, and he would have to spend a lot of time marketing the new platform rather than interacting with followers. “When you do it on your own, you have to start over. You have to tell people where you are.” He also gets to use CNBC’s programming to “help people find the club,” and hopes interest in the club will also strengthen bonds with CNBC.

	One of the keys to the club’s success so far, says Sullivan, is that it focuses on education and the ins-and-outs of the market. Yes, money can result, but learning about how to trade creates a “passion” that is hard to duplicate. Cramer “has really created a model for all of CNBC and how we are thinking about direct to consumer as part of our portfolio,” the executive says. CNBC is also developing a separate digital subscription product for retail investors, which it plans to launch in early 2027.
	

	Cramer gained fame as a savvy trader, and also launched the financial-news site TheStreet.com, but he also knows what less-experienced investors are seeking. “They are not able to whip around and buy Invidia today at 182 and sell it at 187, That’s not their style, but I can tell them” ways to build a solid portfolio. These market followers “don’t want to get in and get out. They want to build positions”

	After years spent playing the market, Cramer wants to pass something on to others. “I want to teach about how things really work” he says. “I can pull the curtain away and show what’s really going on.” In doing so, he may offer a few lessons about the future of the media sector as well.

schema.headline: Jim Cramer Leads CNBC Into Creator-Media Era

title: Joaquin Phoenix Stars in AI Eyewear Campaign Directed by Jonathan Glazer
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Joaquin P
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Joaquin Phoenix is entering the world of wearable AI.

	The Oscar-winning actor stars in a new campaign film for Gentle Monster’s upcoming intelligent eyewear collection, directed by “The Zone of Interest” filmmaker Jonathan Glazer. The South Korean eyewear brand unveiled a first-look teaser Friday, ahead of the collection’s Nov. 12 pre-order launch.

	The surreal short film follows a salesman, played by Phoenix, who encounters a series of bizarre occurrences inside an unfamiliar hotel. He then comes face-to-face with mysterious figures at the end of a red-lit corridor, eventually discovering that his intelligent eyewear allows him to understand and communicate with them. The full film is scheduled to debut later this month.
	



	

	



	The collection is part of a larger partnership between Gentle Monster, Google and Samsung, first unveiled at Google I/O in May. Built on Google’s Android XR platform and powered by its Gemini AI assistant, the smart glasses promise to offer hands-free assistance, allowing users to take photos, make calls and translate conversations.

	Fashion and technology companies have been trying to make AI-powered wearables the next “big thing” for a while. The wave continued with Meta and Ray-Ban’s second generation of AI glasses endorsed by Kylie Jenner earlier this year. Meanwhile, luxury conglomerate Kering, whose portfolio includes Gucci and Saint Laurent, has partnered with Google to develop its own AI-powered eyewear. In April, Kering CEO Luca de Meo said the company was targeting a 2027 debut for Gucci-branded smart glasses.
	

	Pre-orders for the Gentle Monster Intelligent Eyewear Collection begin Nov. 12, followed by a public preview in New York from Nov. 13 to 23. Registration for the preview will be available through the brand’s website.

schema.headline: Joaquin Phoenix Stars in AI Eyewear Campaign Directed by Jonathan Glazer

title: ‘Stranger Things’ Prequel Spinoff ‘Other Worlds’ Ordered to Series at Netflix
description:
The long-gestating “Stranger Things” spinoff has officially been ordered to series at Netflix, Variety has learned. 

	The show is titled “Other Wo
body:
The long-gestating “Stranger Things” spinoff has officially been ordered to series at Netflix, Variety has learned. 

	The show is titled “Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure” and is set to debut in 2028. The announcement comes as part of “Stranger Things” Day, the annual celebration to mark the day Will Byers disappeared in the original show — Nov. 6, 1983. 

	This is now the fourth project set in the “Stranger Things” universe. In addition to the wildly popular mothership show, which ended its run at the end of 2025, there is also the animated series “Stranger Things: Tales from ’85” and the stage show “Stranger Things: First Shadow,” the latter of which delves more into the backstory of Henry Creel, aka Vecna. The spinoff was first reported to be in the works in 2022. 
	

	Plot details are scarce for “Other Worlds,” aside from the fact it will be a prequel set in the 1950’s prior to the events of “Stranger Things” and the “The First Shadow.” In an interview tied to the series finale, Matt and Ross Duffer teased that the spinoff would focus on the events prior to Henry Creel being exposed to the otherworldly substance that gave him his powers in “Stranger Things.” 

	A teaser asset for “Other Worlds” confirmed that, with the video (see below) revealing that the series will take place in 1955 in Marion, Nevada. 

	“Other Worlds” is co-created by the Duffer brothers and Kate Trefry, a writer on “Stranger Things” and the writer of “The First Shadow.” Trefry will also serve as showrunner and executive producer on the series. Joe Wright will direct the first three episodes and executive produce, with Shawn Levy of 21 Laps, Paul Dichter, Shelley Meals, Andrea Sperling, and Pavlina Hatoupis also executive producing. The series will film in New Mexico. 
	

	“We’ve been dreaming of ‘Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure’ for many years now, and to see it become a reality is surreal and exhilarating,” the Duffers said. “We’re so grateful to our incredible team of collaborators: our showrunner Kate Trefry, who has been in the trenches with us since Season 2 and wrote ‘Stranger Things: The First Shadow;’ and our director, Joe Wright, a brilliant artist whose work we’ve long admired. We can’t wait for you to see what they’re cooking up. It’s Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new… actually, we’re not allowed to say any more. Now, on to casting. In the meantime — watch the skies, nerds!”

	The Duffers are executive producing under their Upside Down Pictures banner, with “Other Worlds” serving as a carve out of their current overall deal at Paramount. The Duffers were previously under an overall deal at Netflix, but it was announced in 2025 that they would be moving to Paramount for a deal that covered movies, television and streaming once their Netflix overall expired in April 2026. 

	“The Duffer Brothers gave me my first paying job in Hollywood, and it has been a joy and a fever dream ever since,” Trefry said. “Now, it is my insane honor and privilege to be bringing this new chapter of ‘Stranger Things’ to life alongside them and our incredible director Joe Wright. With the support of Netflix and 21Laps, we have had the time of our lives returning to all the horror, wonder and mystery of the flagship, while also telling a wholly new story, one we hope will blow your minds and break your hearts all over again. There are so many more mysteries to explore. Welcome to ‘Other Worlds.’”

	“’Stranger Things’ has always belonged to the fans, and their passion made it a worldwide phenomenon,” said Jinny Howe, Netflix Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada. “Today, on ‘Stranger Things’ Day, we’re honored to partner again with Matt and Ross Duffer and Kate Trefry to give fans a new dimension of this universe to step into. ‘Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure’ takes us to the 1950s with new heroes and all the heart, mystery, and spectacle of the original series. We’re proud to keep building this world with the Duffers, Kate, Shawn Levy, and Joe Wright, and we can’t wait for fans to see what’s next.”
	

	“All of us at 21Laps are thrilled and privileged to be continuing the storytelling legacy of ‘Stranger Things,” Levy added. “With ‘Other Worlds,’ the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry craft a new ensemble and adventure that is imbued with the DNA of our flagship series while exploring a new era, setting and all-new characters, themes and mythology — the seeds of which may have been planted in Hawkins, but now venture into other worlds of spectacle, action and emotion.”

schema.headline: ‘Stranger Things’ Prequel Spinoff ‘Other Worlds’ Ordered to Series at Netflix

title: Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain ‘Open Ecosystem’
description: Surprise! Fox Corp. said Friday it has closed the acquisition of streaming platform Roku, a deal valued at $22 billion, well ahead of the expected
body:
Surprise! Fox Corp. said Friday it has closed the acquisition of streaming platform Roku, a deal valued at $22 billion, well ahead of the expected 2027 date.  

	Roku founder and CEO Anthony Wood will join the Fox board of directors. He will serve as co-chair, Fox Digital Platforms, a newly formed division that includes Roku, Tubi, Fox One, Red Seat Ventures and other digital products and services across the company, alongside Paul Cheesbrough, who assumes the role of co-chair and CEO of the division.
	

	“The closing of this acquisition advances the long-term strategy of Fox,” Lachlan Murdoch, executive chair and CEO of Fox Corp., said in a statement Friday.

	Fox Corp. emphasized its pledge that it will preserve Roku “as a leading open ecosystem for the broader streaming industry.” That means that, say, it won’t automatically give exclusive or advantageous positioning to Fox News or the Fox One streaming package on Roku, which has a customer base of more than 100 million households.

	The Roku deal will dramatically beef up Fox’s streaming footprint and give it the opportunity to increase scale in the free, ad-supported streaming space through Fox’s Tubi and the Roku Channel. With Roku, Fox overnight is now a much bigger player in digital video advertising as well as key distributor of premium subscription streaming services.

	“Beginning today, our top priority for the combined company is to continue to relentlessly serve audiences and partners, while reinforcing the openness and choice that is the essence of the Roku platform,” Murdoch said. “Our shared entrepreneurial passion and clear conviction toward building the future together with our new Roku colleagues gives us great confidence in the opportunities ahead of us.”
	

	Fox Corp. said it expects to achieve approximately $400 million of annualized cost synergies within two years after the Roku deal close, suggesting layoffs are in the offing. Fox also said there’s potential revenue upside with the combination of Roku’s business and that it anticipates that the acquisition will be accretive to free cash flow per share by the second full year after closing.

	Wood said in a statement: “We started Roku more than two decades ago to give people a better way to watch TV, and that mission doesn’t change today. What does change is our reach and resources. Fox has a deep respect for Roku’s culture and wholly shares our commitment to staying open to every content partner. Our teams will keep building and innovating as they always have, now with the support and capabilities of Fox behind us. I’m proud of what Roku’s employees have built, and I’m excited about what comes next.”

	It certainly behooves Fox Corp. to preserve Roku’s arms-dealer status as a front-end to a ubiquitous array of streaming content and services including Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, HBO Max and more.

	In the first nine months of 2026, Roku has topped financial forecasts, delivering 23% revenue growth for the period to hit $4.1 billion in sales. About 49% of that came from advertising and 40% is from subscriptions. In Q3, Roku’s total gross profit was $649 million, up 24%, and Roku generated net income of $183 million — up more than seven-fold from the year-prior quarter. 

	In June, Fox announced the agreement to buy Roku for $160/share in a combination of about $14.2 billion in cash and the remainder in Fox Class A common stock. Shareholders of both companies approved the deal on Oct. 14.

schema.headline: Fox Closes $22 Billion Roku Takeover, Says Streaming Platform Will Remain ‘Open Ecosystem’

title: Former Top Arkansas Official Arrested for Allegedly Tampering With Bar Exam Scores
description:
Arkansas Official Arrested
                          Allegedly Tampered With Bar Exam Scores
body:
Arkansas Official Arrested
                          Allegedly Tampered With Bar Exam Scores
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 6, 2026
                            7:11 AM PST
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A former top Arkansas official found herself on the wrong side of the law after she was arrested on 65 felonies for allegedly changing bar exam scores over a 5-year period, according to a new report.
      
    
            KATV in Little Rock reports that Nancie Givens was charged with 65 counts of tampering with a public record. Givens was the former executive director of the Arkansas Office of Professional Programs, which is in charge of protecting the accuracy of bar exam records.
      
    
            Arkansas State Police launched a probe into the matter years ago and found a boatload of irregularities in bar exams given to aspiring lawyers between July 2020 and July 2025.
      
    
            Investigators learned that Givens allegedly altered or deleted about 11,400 electronic files pertaining to Arkansas Bar applicant records, profiles, and score sheets that the Office of Professional Programs is required by law to retain for 25 years.
      
    
            Why did she allegedly do it? Nobody knows except Givens, who hasn't said a word about it yet.
      
    
            Givens resigned from her position in February after investigators discovered the alleged irregularities in January. The allegations against Givens raise questions as to the integrity of the bar exams administered during that 5-year period.
      
    
            Sixth Judicial District Prosecuting Attorney Will Jones wouldn't say how many bar exams were affected, whether any applicants were impacted, or if Givens' alleged crimes changed the outcome of bar admissions.

Thomas Markle
                          Arrested Over Child Sex Abuse Material

            Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr., has been arrested in Florida for possession of child sexual abuse material ... following weeks of disturbing allegations ... TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            FBI agents arrested the 82-year-old at his senior living facility in Lakeland.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the Daily Mail, the bust came after the outlet alerted federal authorities to alleged child sexual abuse material discovered in an abandoned storage unit he rented in Mexico.
      

            As TMZ previously reported ... authorities raided the storage unit in Rosarito, Mexico, where investigators reportedly seized computers, thumb drives, VHS tapes and other materials after reports raised concerns about its contents.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Thomas was already under investigation in the Philippines after authorities uncovered thousands of alleged child sexual abuse images linked to his former home.
      
    
            Philippine Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla revealed Thursday that investigators recovered roughly 7,500 photos and a video depicting alleged sexual abuse of boys and girls of Asian, Latin American and European descent ... some as young as 10 or 11.
      
    
            Remulla described the material as "deplorable" ... though authorities have not determined who owned the devices containing the images.
      
    
            Thomas previously denied the allegations, calling them "sick lies."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The investigation began after Thomas' son, Thomas Markle Jr., claimed he discovered hundreds, if not thousands, of disturbing images among his father's belongings at his former home in Cebu.
      
    
            In another twist ... Thomas Jr. has since been named a person of interest in the Philippine investigation, though authorities stressed he is not currently considered a suspect.
      
    
            Meghan previously said she was "deeply distressed" by the allegations against her father ... claiming she'd received troubling information about him years earlier and kept him away from her children to protect them.
      
    
            Story developing ...

            Katy Perry's name was nearly introduced during Russell Brand's rape trial -- but prosecutors ultimately decided to spike the idea of discussing the ex-couple's marriage as part of their opening statement ... after he raised objections.
      
    
            Citing pre-trial proceedings, The Telegraph reports that prosecutors wanted to mention Russell's relationship with Katy in their opening statement.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            But Russell's defense attorneys were able to successfully block prosecutors from uttering Katy's name and referencing her relationship to him because the details were irrelevant to the case.
      

            As you may know, Russell tied the knot with Katy in October 2010 ... he filed for divorce in December 2011 ... and in July 2012 the divorce was finalized.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            On Thursday ... Russell was found guilty of raping a young fan and sexually assaulting 3 women after a 4-week trial at London's Southwark Crown Court.
      
    
            Russell was immediately taken into custody, and he now awaits sentencing on Monday ... with a lengthy prison sentence a possibility.

title: Dolly Parton's Manager Voluntarily Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
description:
Dolly Parton's Manager
                          Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
body:
Dolly Parton's Manager
                          Dismisses Lawsuit Against Her Nephew
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
          Update
  
    
            3:34 PM PT -- Bryan Seaver's attorney, Dominic J. Leonardo, tells TMZ ... "Mr. Seaver cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the incredible legacy she left behind. He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his entire family. Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly's legacy remains entirely untouched."
      
    
            Dolly Parton's nephew Bryan Seaver just scored a major legal victory ... because the late legend's manager has dropped the lawsuit against him.
      
    
            According to Rolling Stone, Danny Nozell filed a notice of voluntary dismissal of his lawsuit Thursday ... in the suit, Danny alleged Bryan had threatened Dolly's business empire.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The dismissal comes before a hearing scheduled for Tuesday ... and before Danny needed to respond to Bryan's denial of the allegations.
      

            It's unclear why Danny pulled the plug on the suit ... or if he and Bryan reached a settlement.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            As we previously reported ... Dolly's nephew asked the judge to dismiss the case against him ... claiming he'd never threatened Danny and the texts he'd sent him had been in jest.
      
    
            Bryan's not completely out of the woods ... Danny dismissed the lawsuit without prejudice ... meaning it could be brought again.
      
    
            Stay tuned ...
